I have been farming these 13.1 mu for twenty years, and I know every corner of them. With my husband and children working part-time off the farm, our labor is tight during the busy seasons, so I must plan carefully. I will put 10 mu into my reliable wheat–maize rotation and keep 3.1 mu for cotton. The wheat–maize system gives us grain we can sell to the grain station at stable prices and feeds our household; cotton earns more cash per mu, but it is labor-heavy, so I cannot expand it beyond what my own two hands can manage at picking time.

For the winter wheat on those 10 mu, I will sow an improved short-stalk variety in early October after rotary tillage. I will spread compound fertilizer at sowing and top-dress urea at green-up. I will irrigate three times from the well—before winter, at jointing, and at grain-filling—because electricity for pumping is expensive and I must not waste water. Two pesticide sprays will be enough: one herbicide at sowing and one insecticide in spring if aphids appear. I expect about 500 kg per mu if late spring does not turn dry.

For summer maize on the same 10 mu, timing is everything. After the wheat harvest in early June, I have only a few days to get the maize in the ground before the rains stop, so I will use no-tillage direct seeding with hybrid seed. I will apply fertilizer at sowing and side-dress more nitrogen at the big-trumpet stage. Two irrigations—one at tasseling and one at grain-filling—are enough in most summers, because July and August usually bring some rain. Two sprays will handle any armyworm or rust. I expect around 580 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 3.1 mu, I will rotary-till in mid-April and plant improved Bt cotton seed under plastic mulch to keep the soil warm and hold moisture. Cotton is hungry for potassium, so I give it a bit more potash than the grain crops. I will irrigate three times—at flowering, peak boll-setting, and early boll-opening—and spray four times for aphids and spider mites that still attack Bt cotton. Picking will take my spare time in autumn, but seed-cotton prices have been decent, so it is worth the trouble. I expect about 240 kg of seed cotton per mu.
